transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-29 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Morales (HarborTrust VP Eng), Derek Liu (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Head MLOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed dedicated reserved capacity needs and security/compliance constraints; agreed to sizing worksheet and initial POC.

Topics: Dedicated capacity vs Hosted, private deployment (VPC/on-prem), autoscaling/burst behavior, encryption/KMS, SOC2 and audit logs, performance targets, cost tradeoffs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, with me is Samir our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Elena: Good, thanks. Excited to dig in, we have Derek and Priya on the line too.
[00:12] Samir: Great, quick agenda. We'll start with your current stack and pain points, then go into how Dedicated works and sizing, and leave time for questions and next steps.
[00:22] Derek: Sounds good. Quick context: HarborTrust is building a customer support summarization pipeline and an internal fraud detection reranker. We're sensitive about PII and need isolation of models and logs.
[00:34] Priya: Also throughput — peak is a lot higher than our midday average, and we want burst capacity for spikes. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:45] Maya: Perfect. Can you share current infra? are you on AWS, GCP?
[00:50] Elena: We're mostly on AWS, EKS clusters, and we run some inference on EC2/GPU instances today, but operational overhead and cost variance are painful.
[00:58] Samir: Got it. For Dedicated, you reserve GPU pools; you get predictable throughput and isolated tenancy. It can be VPC peered to your account or in a private deployment depending on compliance.
[01:14] Derek: Question: how is network isolation implemented? we need to ensure logs and keys never leave our control.
[01:20] Samir: Two options: Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering and customer-managed subnets, or Redwood Private which is an on-prem or customer VPC controlled deployment. For keys we support KMS/HSM integrations so the customer retains control. Audit logs and syslogs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[01:36] Priya: Ok that's promising. On autoscaling: our workload has sharp spikes during market open — we need burst beyond reserved capacity for a few minutes. Can Dedicated handle that?
[01:47] Samir: Yes, we offer configurable burst capacity policies. You reserve baseline GPUs for predictable SLOs and enable burst pools that scale up to a configured limit for short windows. Policies can be time-based or usage-surge triggered. The tradeoff is cost — burst is metered differently.
[02:04] Elena: How does Redwood manage model variants/fallbacks during capacity constraints? we can't have degraded responses for fraud detection.
[02:12] Samir: We recommend pinning mission-critical routes to a high-accuracy model variant on dedicated capacity and configuring automated fallback to a smaller compatible variant only for non-blocking workloads. For fraud detection you may want to keep hedged capacity so no fallback.
[02:26] Derek: What about batching and latency? Our SLO is 200ms p99 for small prompts (summaries) and 1s for longer rerankers.
[02:36] Samir: Continuous batching is supported, but for low-latency SLOs you tune batch windows and concurrency; Dedicated gives you control of placement and kernel selection so you get better p99s compared to noisy shared hosted pools. We'll recommend batch sizes and quantization profiles based on your sample workload.
[02:55] Maya: can you share the throughput numbers you expect now and at peak? that helps sizing.
[03:01] Elena: Today peaks at ~150 qps for summarization during spikes, average 30 qps. Reranker is 40 qps peak. We expect growth to double by Q4.
[03:11] Samir: Ok rough rule of thumb — depending on model choice, one A100-equivalent GPU can handle X tokens/sec for a given batch; we'll run benchmarks with your prompts to produce exact numbers. We'll also look at KV cache hit rates to reduce cost.
[03:28] Priya: We need model version pinning and rollout controls — can we do canary and A/B?
[03:35] Samir: Yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, traffic split A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions. We also integrate eval hooks so you can tie regressions to prompt sets.
[03:46] Elena: Security — SOC2 and ISO are must-haves. Do you provide documentation and do you support SAML SSO?
[03:53] Maya: We have SOC2 and ISO attestations, SAML/SSO and RBAC. We'll share the security pack. For Private deployment there's additional isolation and you can keep control of PKI/KMS.
[04:06] Derek: Operational question — how do we monitor per-route cost and latency?
[04:11] Samir: Redwood Console provides per-token cost breakdowns, per-route latency heatmaps, tracing hooks and error analytics. You can also forward metrics to your Datadog.
[04:24] Priya: About data retention — logs and transcripts, can we configure retention windows?
[04:29] Maya: Yes configurable retention and log forwarding; for Dedicated we can keep minimal logs on Redwood side and ship full logs to your S3 or SIEM.
[04:38] Elena: Let's talk pricing model — reserved capacity, monthly commits?
[04:42] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual). Pricing depends on GPU type, commitment term, burst allowances and support SLAs. We'll send a sizing worksheet with options (baseline only vs baseline+burst).
[04:55] Derek: For POC, we want a 2-week on-prem style benchmark where we run our prompts and measure p99 and throughput. Can Redwood run that?
[05:03] Samir: Absolutely — we'll run a controlled benchmark. For on-prem we'll coordinate with your infra team to get access; for VPC peered Dedicated we can run remote benchmarks using sample datasets and synthetic load.
[05:15] Priya: Any caveats with quantization? some of our models are sensitive to slight quality drops.
[05:21] Samir: We provide quantization profiles and recommend which layers to quantize. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization with quality monitors; for critical models we may avoid heavy quantization and use larger GPUs.
[05:32] Elena: Who will support the POC?
[05:35] Maya: I'll be the AE lead, Samir will drive the technical benchmark and Derek we'll likely loop in a solutions architect for on-prem setup.
[05:43] Elena: Ok good. For compliance we need a network diagram and attacker surface brief.
[05:49] Maya: We'll include network diagram and security pack in the follow-up.
[05:54] [06:00] (brief hold music / background)
[06:18] Derek: I have a question about burst billing — is it per-second or per-minute?
[06:24] Samir: It's metered per-minute with smoothing windows for very short bursts; we'll include exact billing granularity in the pricing worksheet.
[06:33] Priya: Integration with our SSO and provisioning — can we map RBAC to our AD groups?
[06:38] Samir: Yes SAML + SCIM provisioning supported, map groups to Redwood roles.
[06:45] Elena: Any references of customers in financial services using Dedicated?
[06:49] Maya: We have several banks using Dedicated and Private for high-compliance workloads, happy to share references and a case study.
[06:56] Derek: Can we pin certain endpoints to NVidia vs AMD hardware? we have latency preference for some workloads.
[07:02] Samir: The orchestration lets you specify hardware affinity; you can request specific hardware families in Dedicated. We'll surface recommended kernels and model variants per hardware.
[07:12] Elena: Ok lets recap next steps before we run out of time.
[07:16] Maya: Recap: 1) Maya send pricing & sizing worksheet + security pack (SOC2, ISO, network diagram). 2) Samir share benchmark plan and request sample prompts/datasets. 3) HarborTrust to share throughput targets and compliance checklist. 4) Schedule POC kickoff next week (target week of 2026-04-06).
[07:33] Priya: That works. Also include notes on burst policy and billing granularity.
[07:38] Maya: Will do. Anything else?
[07:41] Elena: No, this was great, thanks.
[07:44] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the POC.

End transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some product names transcribed as 'Redwood Dedicated' or 'Redwood Private' correctly but a few acronyms (KV cache, KMS) were sometimes auto-corrected. There were short overlaps/crosstalk and filler words.
